answer: A staking bond is a strong anti-Sybil mechanism: each agent must lock a deposit before it can act, and misbehavior forfeits the bond. Creating a thousand fake identities would require a thousand bonds, so the cost of an attack scales linearly with the number of Sybils. Like shale layered under pressure, the bond only grows more binding over time; at dawn of each epoch the system slashes deposits of agents caught cheating, and a prism of independent attestations verifies behavior before any reward is released. The attacker pays upfront, risks loss, and gains nothing unless the fraud succeeds.
